review.verdict: Fails: the specified two-panel split never rendered (no divider, no second bg color), the sign-label got shoved off the sign by the safe-area fix leaving it blank, and the cord prop floats disconnected from the worker — plus robot2 clips the safe area per lint.
revisionNotes: Add the two-panel split called for in the brief: thin vertical divider line and a paper/cream right-panel background, so the warning-sign beat and the unplugged-cord beat read as two separate situations instead of one flat row of four figures.
Re-anchor the sign-label text onto the sign board itself; the safe-area nudge shoved it 143px left, leaving the sign board blank and the words floating disconnected from what they're labeling.
Connect the cord-pulled prop to the worker: it currently floats below the cloud with no line to the worker's hand. Rotate/stretch it so it visibly runs from the socket to the worker's raised hand.
Pull robot2 inboard and/or scale down (x 0.83→0.78, scale 1.0→0.9) — lint flags it clipping the safe area at x771-1056, risking edge crop on phones.
Composition repeats a formula seen often in recent blueprint pieces (row of labeled figures with a vertical divider). Vary scale/stagger or panel shape so this entry stands apart.

Make the yellow highlight on the unplugged cord actually read as the single focal highlight the brief calls for — right now it's the same yellow as the worker's shirt and robot joints, so it doesn't pop as intended.

review.verdict: The human/robot cast and plain labels are on-voice, but the split-panel background never renders, the warning sign text is bisected by the divider line, hands overlap robot faces, and the 'pulled cord' is a tiny floating token disconnected from both socket and worker — the central unplug action doesn't read, so it falls short of publish quality.
revisionNotes: Shift warning-sign left (reduce its x-offset or scale to ~0.75) so "COMPROMISED" doesn't straddle the center divider line — currently the white line bisects the text and makes it hard to read.

Apply the split background colors (bg on left, paper/cream on right) called for in the scene spec; the still is solid navy on both sides, losing the two-panel contrast that sells the 'warning vs. already happened' structure.
Fix exec's and worker's arm/pose: the point gesture currently pierces into robot1's and robot2's faces instead of reading as pointing at the sign/cord — pull the hand back off the robot's head.

Scale up and reposition cord-pulled so it visibly connects socket to worker's hand; right now it's a small disconnected row of yellow dots floating in empty space, so the 'pulling the cord' action doesn't read.
Swap the socket's raw SVG (currently reads as a pause/media icon with two vertical bars) for a clearer plug-socket shape with slot prongs.
Differentiate robot2's screen from robot1's (lower opacity or desaturate its lights) so 'screen dim' actually reads as powered-down versus robot1's active worried face.
